name: The Deadmines
summary: Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hide the Defias Brotherhood's staging ground. Once a source of the kingdom’s gold, the tunnels were abandoned in the First War and long feared as haunted. Edwin VanCleef and goblin engineers now work there beyond the realm’s eyes, building an engine of vengeance against Stormwind.

sections.title: A Legacy of Gold and Ruin
sections.body:
Before the First War, the Deadmines were called the greatest gold-producing center in human lands. Their gold supplied a third of Stormwind’s reserves. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to darkness.

Sir Anduin Lothar spent twenty months imprisoned by subterranean ogres while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity. Warchief Blackhand’s rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages with the ogre Turok, and both met their ends there. Believed cursed and home only to shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.

sections.title: Sanctum of the Brotherhood
sections.body:
After the Stonemasons’ Guild was cast out of Stormwind without payment for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef gathered the disgruntled artisans into the Defias Brotherhood. Seeking a secure headquarters beyond the reach of Gryan Stoutmantle’s People’s Militia, the Brotherhood chose its central redoubt in the abandoned tunnels.

They drove out the legitimate Miners’ League, leaving Foreman Thistlenettle’s doomed workers to perish and rise as undead ghouls. Lumbering ogres, seasoned brigands, and mechanical constructs guard the shafts, now an industrial war camp. Picks, fires, and illicit industry echo through the lower mines once more.

sections.title: The Secret of Ironclad Cove
sections.body:
Beyond the sweltering Goblin Foundry and timber-strewn Mast Room, Ironclad Cove opens beneath the Dagger Hills. There, VanCleef employed goblin shipbuilders and tinkerers to construct a colossal ironclad dreadnaught. Captain Greenskin commands the warship, with First Mate Mr. Smite beside him.

The ship is designed to pass through an underwater sea gate toward the ocean. There, the Defias Brotherhood means to prey on the sea trade that keeps Stormwind rich.

faq.q: Where is the entrance to the Deadmines located?
faq.answer: The entrance lies inside a derelict barn in ruined Moonbrook, southwestern Westfall. Winding tunnels cross an outer complex of Defias diggers and undead miners before reaching the locked instance threshold.

faq.q: Why does everyone call the Deadmines 'VC'?
faq.answer: Adventurers call the dungeon “VC” after its master, Edwin VanCleef. The shorthand avoids confusion with Dire Maul in Feralas, an ancient elven complex that shares the initials “DM.”

Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant guildmaster of the Stonemasons, who oversaw Stormwind City’s majestic reconstruction after the First War. When the House of Nobles refused to pay its debts, VanCleef formed the Defias Brotherhood to demand restitution through rebellion and open brigandage.

faq.q: What is being built in Ironclad Cove?
faq.answer: The Defias are building a massive ironclad juggernaut in Ironclad Cove. They contracted goblin engineers to assemble it with heavy ordnance and sturdy timber, so it can sail through the cove’s sea gate and raid the trade that feeds the capital.

faq.q: What happened to the Miners' League workers outside the instance?
faq.answer: Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew were sent to legally reopen the mines for the kingdom. When the Defias stormed the works, a tunnel collapse trapped the miners in the dark. They starved there and eventually rose as mindless, restless undead.

faq.q: What does defeating Cookie the murloc mean for the Defias ship?
faq.answer: Cookie is the bizarre ship’s cook aboard VanCleef’s dreadnaught. Defeating VanCleef cuts off the rebellion’s head. Slaying Cookie clears the remaining crew from the ship’s galley and breaks the crew’s presence in Ironclad Cove before you escape through the coastal passage.

faq.q: Where does the exit tunnel lead when leaving the dungeon?
faq.answer: The natural tunnel behind the dreadnaught leads to an exit along the coastal bluffs of the Dagger Hills. From there, you look out toward the ocean and the Westfall Lighthouse.

angles.text: For the Alliance, the Deadmines are Stormwind’s gravest internal threat. Bringing down VanCleef is the defining victory that restores hope to Westfall’s besieged farmers.
As a paladin, you face a test of valor and faith in these desecrated shafts. They echo the historic trials of Sir Anduin Lothar and the lost miners whose restless dead still wander the outer tunnels.
As a miner, you find rocky tunnels that once supplied a third of the capital’s wealth. Veins of copper, tin, and precious silver still run through them.
As an engineer, you can study the Goblin Foundry and Sneed’s mechanical workshop. They show cutting-edge steam shredders, remote-controlled golems, and specialized ordnance.
